mainTopic: Whether one who offers outside the עזרה an animal that was invalidly slaughtered inside (at night) is liable, and עולא's rule about אימורים of קדשים קלים placed on the מזבח before זריקת הדם
overview: This amud opens by finishing רבי יוחנן's argument: someone who slaughters an animal at night and offers it outside is liable, because his case is no better than slaughtering and offering outside. רב חייא בר אבין challenges him from a משנה that exempts someone who slaughters a bird inside and offers it outside. The גמרא calls this a תיובתא, then adds that a bird slaughtered inside may count as simply killed. Next, עולא rules that אימורים of קדשים קלים put on the מזבח before זריקת הדם do not come down, because they have become the 'bread of the מזבח'. רבי זירא tries to prove this from the משנה's list, but the גמרא limits that list to קדשי קדשים and explains the פסח there as slaughtered שלא לשמן. A second proof, from 'all of them that went up alive come down', is also pushed off: that line is about live animals with a small eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא. This raises a question about the משנה's next clause, which says an עולה slaughtered on top of the מזבח is flayed and cut there. The גמרא explains that clause in two ways, depending on whether flaying on top of the מזבח is allowed. It ends by explaining why the innards are taken down and rinsed: so they are not offered with their dung.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reasoning: no better than slaughtering outside
steps.stepSummary: The last line of רבי יוחנן's argument. Slaughtering at night and offering outside should be treated no less strictly than slaughtering outside and offering outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should not be less strict than one who slaughters outside and offers up outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's argument from the previous daf. He explains why someone who slaughtered at night and offered outside is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal slaughtered outside the עזרה could never be brought on the מזבח in the עזרה, yet offering it outside still makes a person חייב. So an animal slaughtered at night, which is also unfit, should make him חייב too. רבי יוחנן reasons from the outside case to the night case.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not be less (strict than)
One who slaughters outside the עזרה
One who offers up outside the עזרה

phrases.english: It should not be less [strict]
phrases.notes: This is the end of רבי יוחנן's argument from the previous daf, about an animal slaughtered at night and then offered outside.

phrases.english: than one who slaughters outside and offers up outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תְּהֵא פְּחוּתָה מִשּׁוֹחֵט בַּחוּץ וּמַעֲלֶה בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's statement begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who slaughters at night and offers outside is חייב, because his case is no better than one who slaughters and offers outside.

steps.title: Challenge from a bird slaughtered inside and offered outside
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין quotes a משנה. A bird slaughtered inside and offered outside makes the person exempt, while one slaughtered outside and offered outside makes him liable. By רבי יוחנן's logic, the first should also be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין objected: One who slaughters a bird inside and offers it up outside is exempt. One who slaughters it outside and offers it up outside is liable. But let us say: it should not be less strict than one who slaughters and offers up outside!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין attacks רבי יוחנן using a משנה about birds. The משנה exempts the person in a case where רבי יוחנן's reasoning would make him liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird slaughtered inside is unfit, just like an animal slaughtered at night. If 'it should be no better than slaughtering outside' were a good argument, the bird case should be חייב too. Yet the משנה says פטור, so the logic seems to fail.

phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Avin raised an objection:
One who slaughters a bird inside
and offers it up outside is exempt.
If he slaughtered outside and offered up outside, he is liable.
Let us say: it should not be less [strict]
than one who slaughters and offers up outside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's argument that an unfit slaughter offered outside is no better than slaughtering outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same argument would make one who slaughters a bird inside and offers it outside חייב, but the משנה rules him פטור.

steps.title: The objection stands as a refutation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that רבי יוחנן is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the challenge works and declares רבי יוחנן's statement refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תיובתא means the objection from the משנה is accepted as decisive. Still, the גמרא goes on in the next step to offer a possible way out.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the objection of step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's argument is refuted by the משנה about the bird.

steps.title: Possible defense: slaughtering a bird inside is just killing it
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the bird case is different. Slaughtering a bird inside with a knife counts as simply killing it, so it cannot be compared to an animal slaughtered at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say: the slaughter of a bird inside — he simply killed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way to defend רבי יוחנן after all. The bird case is different, because slaughtering a bird inside counts as mere killing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal slaughtered at night is unfit, but it still counts as a slaughtered קרבן. A bird slaughtered inside counts only as an act of killing, so it stands further away from a real offering. Because of that difference, the bird משנה does not disprove רבי יוחנן's logic for the night case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (an alternative answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא takes back the word תיובתא. It is only adding a possible way that רבי יוחנן could still be defended.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
the slaughter of a bird inside —
he simply killed it.
phrases.notes: A bird offering is supposed to be done by מליקה (pinching the neck), so using a knife inside counts as just killing it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: שְׁחִיטַת הָעוֹף בִּפְנִים מִיקְטָל קַטְלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a defense of רבי יוחנן against the refutation in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bird slaughtered inside and an animal slaughtered at night are both just unfit slaughters, so they should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Slaughtering a bird inside counts as mere killing, while an animal slaughtered at night still counts as slaughtered. So רבי יוחנן's comparison can still hold for the animal.

steps.title: עולא: אימורים offered before זריקת הדם do not come down
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules on אימורים of קדשים קלים placed on the מזבח before their blood was thrown. They do not come down, because they have become the 'bread of the מזבח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Sacrificial parts of offerings of lesser holiness that one put up on the altar before their blood was thrown shall not come down; they have become the bread of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling from עולא about items put on the מזבח too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the אימורים of קדשים קלים become ready for the מזבח through זריקת הדם. עולא says that even if they were brought up before that, once they are on the מזבח they stay there. The מזבח has 'taken hold' of them as its food.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial parts burned on the מזבח
Throwing their blood on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new discussion about which items, once placed on the מזבח, stay there even though they were not yet fit.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Sacrificial parts of offerings of lesser holiness
that one put up [on the altar] before the throwing of their blood —
shall not come down,
they have become the bread of the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: אֵימוּרֵי קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים שֶׁהֶעֱלָן לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about items placed on the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אימורים of קדשים קלים placed on the מזבח before זריקת הדם do not come down, because they have become the bread of the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי זירא brings support for עולא from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא points to the משנה's cases of blood that was spilled or taken outside the curtains. If those parts don't come down, then surely parts whose blood can still be thrown don't come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: We also learned this in the משנה. The list of things that stay on the מזבח once they went up includes an offering whose blood was spilled, and one whose blood went out beyond the curtains. Now, in that case, even if he wants to throw the blood he has nothing to throw, and still you said: if they went up, they do not come down. So here, where the blood is still there and he can throw it, isn't it all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is supporting עולא's ruling from step 5 with a line of the משנה and a כל שכן argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case the blood is gone, so the parts can never become permitted by זריקה, yet they still stay on the מזבח. In עולא's case the blood is still there and can be thrown. So the parts are in a better position, and they should certainly stay on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned it (in a משנה): a phrase used to bring support
The curtains around the courtyard of the משכן, standing for the boundary of the holy area
Throwing the blood on the מזבח, the step that makes the offering acceptable
If they went up (onto the מזבח), they do not come down
All the more so: a stronger-case argument

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
We too have learned this:
[an offering] whose blood was spilled,
and one whose blood went out beyond the curtains.
Now, if there, where if he comes to throw [the blood]
he has nothing to throw,
you said: if they went up, they do not come down;
then here, where if he comes to throw, he can throw,
phrases.notes: "Here" means עולא's case, where the blood simply hasn't been thrown yet.

phrases.english: is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the משנה for עולא's ruling in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's ruling that אימורים of קדשים קלים put on the מזבח before זריקה do not come down
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's list including שנשפך דמה and שיצא דמה חוץ לקלעים, used in a כל שכן

steps.title: The proof is limited to the most holy offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's spilled-blood cases may be talking only about קדשי קדשים, so they prove nothing about קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain that line of the משנה as talking about קדשי קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבי זירא's proof by saying the משנה he quoted may only be about קדשי קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's ruling is specifically about קדשים קלים. If the משנה's spilled-blood cases are only about קדשי קדשים, then רבי זירא's כל שכן doesn't reach עולא's case. קדשים קלים could be treated differently before their blood is thrown.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain it as (referring to): limits a source to a specific case
Offerings of the highest holiness (like עולה and חטאת)

phrases.english: Explain it as referring to the most holy offerings.
phrases.notes: "It" means the משנה's cases of spilled blood that רבי זירא just quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the proof in step 6 by narrowing the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the spilled-blood cases of the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may refer only to קדשי קדשים, while עולא's ruling concerns קדשים קלים

steps.title: But the פסח in the list is a lesser offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the limit: the same list in the משנה includes the פסח, which is קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסח is listed there, and it is קדשים קלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 7: how can the list be only about קדשי קדשים if it includes the פסח?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח is a קדשים קלים offering. Since it appears in the same list, the list seems to include קדשים קלים too, which would bring back רבי זירא's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: But look: points to something that contradicts what was just said

phrases.english: But there is the פסח, and it is a lesser offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit set in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה refers only to קדשי קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The list includes the פסח, which is קדשים קלים, so it cannot be limited to קדשי קדשים

steps.title: The פסח case is about wrong intent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסח in the list is about one slaughtered שלא לשמן, not about spilled blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain the פסח case as one slaughtered not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the limit by giving the פסח in the list its own separate case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח is in the list because of a different problem, being slaughtered שלא לשמן. The spilled-blood cases can still be about קדשי קדשים only. So רבי זירא's proof stays blocked.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own sake: slaughtered with the intention of a different offering

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's proof from the spilled-blood cases is pushed off. Those cases can be explained as only about קדשי קדשים, and the פסח in the list is about שלא לשמן.

phrases.english: Explain it as one slaughtered not for its own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסח in the list shows that the spilled-blood cases include קדשים קלים
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסח is listed only for the case of שלא לשמן, so the spilled-blood cases can still be only about קדשי קדשים

steps.title: A new proof from animals that went up alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה: animals that went up alive come down. That suggests slaughtered ones do not come down, apparently with no difference between קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: and all of them, if they went up onto the מזבח alive, they come down. That suggests that if they were slaughtered, they do not come down. Doesn't that mean there is no difference between קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new attempt to support עולא from a different line of the משנה. It is a question looking for an answer, setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From "alive ones come down" we can infer that slaughtered ones stay up, even before their blood was thrown. The משנה says this about all offerings without dividing them. So it seems to include קדשים קלים too, which would support עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? Opens a suggested proof

phrases.english: We learned: and all of them that went up alive
onto the מזבח, they come down.
This implies that slaughtered ones do not come down;
phrases.notes: Even if their blood wasn't thrown yet, which is exactly עולא's case.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי, לָאו לָא שְׁנָא קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים
phrases.english: Isn't it that it makes no difference whether most holy offerings
or lesser offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁעָלוּ חַיִּין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ – יֵרְדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was blocked, starts a new proof attempt for עולא from another line of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's ruling about אימורים of קדשים קלים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from the משנה's line וכולן שעלו חיין לגבי מזבח ירדו: slaughtered ones do not come down, with no distinction between kinds of offerings

steps.title: Slaughtered ones: some come down, some don't
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference from the live-animal line. Slaughtered animals are not one uniform group, so no proof can be drawn about קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. You can infer this instead: slaughtered ones, some of them come down and some of them don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 10. It says the line about live animals does not tell us that every slaughtered animal stays up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 read 'live ones come down' as 'slaughtered ones never come down,' with no difference between kinds of קדשים. Here the גמרא says the opposite inference is only partial: among slaughtered ones, some come down and some don't. So we still can't tell which group קדשים קלים before זריקה belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that have already been slaughtered
They shall come down (be taken off the מזבח)

phrases.english: No; but slaughtered ones —
some of them come down, some of them do not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in Step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that all slaughtered animals stay on the מזבח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The opposite of 'live ones come down' can be 'some slaughtered ones stay,' not 'all slaughtered ones stay'

steps.title: But the משנה says 'all of them'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 11. The משנה says 'all of them' come down if alive, which suggests that all of them stay if slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches 'all of them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection in Step 11 by pointing to the word 'all' in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'all of them' come down when alive, it sounds like 'all of them' stay when slaughtered, with no exceptions. That would bring back the proof from Step 10.

phrases.english: But it teaches "all of them"!
phrases.notes: This points to the משנה's line: all of them that went up alive to the top of the מזבח come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only some slaughtered ones stay up
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'all' implies a blanket rule, so its opposite should be a blanket rule too

steps.title: 'All of them' refers only to live animals
steps.stepSummary: The word 'all' covers only the live-animal case. It says nothing about every slaughtered animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'All of them' is about the live ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'all' only describes the live animals. Every live one comes down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All' stresses that no live animal stays on the מזבח. You cannot flip it into a rule that every slaughtered animal stays.

keyTerms.meaning: About live ones (animals that went up alive)

phrases.english: "All of them" refers to the live ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'All' sets a rule for slaughtered animals too
steps.terutzMaskana: 'All' only stresses that every live animal comes down

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: If the line only teaches that live animals come down, that seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה would need to teach that live animals come down. That seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A live animal was never offered at all, so of course it should be taken down. The answer in Step 13 seems to leave the משנה teaching nothing new.

phrases.english: It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 13 as making the משנה pointless
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'all of them' is only about live animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה would be teaching something nobody doubted

steps.title: Live animals with a small eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The line is about live animals with a small blemish on the eye. רבי עקיבא holds such animals stay up once they went up. The משנה teaches that if they went up alive, they still come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it's about live ones, but ones with a blemish on the eye's cornea. It follows רבי עקיבא, who says if they went up they don't come down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the line is not obvious. It is about animals with a tiny eye blemish, and it follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא says animals with a small eye blemish that went up on the מזבח are not taken down. You might think that applies even if they went up alive. The משנה teaches that even רבי עקיבא agrees live ones come down.

keyTerms.meaning: Small blemishes on the cornea of the eye

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean every live animal case is about blemishes. The גמרא is explaining why the משנה needed to say 'live ones come down' at all.

phrases.english: Really it is about live ones —
but with small blemishes in the eye;
phrases.notes: A tiny blemish on the cornea of the eye.

phrases.english: and according to רבי עקיבא,
who said: if they went up, they do not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Live animals coming down is too obvious to teach
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is live animals with an eye blemish. Even רבי עקיבא agrees they come down.

steps.title: The next clause: a live עולה slaughtered on top is flayed and cut there
steps.stepSummary: If the line is about disqualified animals, the next clause can't fit. A disqualified animal can't be flayed and cut, but the clause says to flay and cut it on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain it, as disqualified animals? Then look at the next clause: 'Likewise, an עולה that went up alive to the top of the מזבח comes down. If he slaughtered it on top of the מזבח, he flays it and cuts it up in its place.' If it is disqualified, can it be flayed and cut? The תורה says 'and he shall cut it.' 'It' means a kosher one, not a disqualified one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks Step 15 using the משנה's next clause. That clause doesn't fit a disqualified animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 made the line about blemished, disqualified animals. The next clause continues 'likewise' and says to flay and cut the animal if it was slaughtered on top. But the פסוק 'and he shall cut it' limits flaying and cutting to kosher offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you set up (explain) it?

phrases.english: How did you explain it — as disqualified ones?
Say the later clause:
And likewise, an עולה that went up alive
to the top of the מזבח — it comes down,
if he slaughtered it on top of the מזבח —
he flays it and cuts it up in its place.
And if it is disqualified —
is it fit for flaying and cutting?!
"And he shall cut it," says the Torah,
"it" — a kosher one, and not a disqualified one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case setup of Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה's live-animal line is about disqualified (blemished) animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The next clause, linked by 'likewise,' calls for flaying and cutting. The פסוק says only kosher offerings get that.

steps.title: The later clause is about a kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the later clause switches to a kosher עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the later clause we've come to a kosher one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the משנה's later clause is about a different case: a kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line can be about blemished animals. The 'likewise' clause moves to a kosher עולה, so flaying and cutting fits it. The two clauses don't have to share the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: We have come to (the case switches to)

phrases.english: In the later clause we have come to a kosher one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the clauses into different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses must be about the same disqualified animal
steps.terutzMaskana: The later clause is about a kosher עולה

steps.title: What is the later clause teaching?
steps.stepSummary: If the later clause is about a kosher עולה, what new thing does it teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what lesson the later clause has, now that it's about a kosher animal. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kosher live animal coming down is plain. So the clause must be teaching something else, and the גמרא wants to know what.

phrases.english: And what does it teach us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the purpose of the clause as explained in Step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The new point of the later clause about a kosher עולה

steps.title: Flaying and cutting may be done on top of the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The clause teaches that flaying and cutting may be done on top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: That flaying and cutting may be done on top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the lesson is about the second half of the clause. If the animal was slaughtered on top, you may flay and cut it right there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think flaying and cutting on the מזבח is improper and the animal must be taken down first. The משנה teaches that this work may be done right there on top.
steps.whatToRemember: The line 'all of them that went up alive come down' does not prove that all slaughtered ones stay up. It is about live animals with an eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא. The later clause is about a kosher עולה and teaches that flaying and cutting may be done on top of the מזבח.

phrases.english: That there is flaying and cutting
on top of the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause teaches that flaying and cutting may be done on top of the מזבח

steps.title: What about the opinion that forbids flaying on top of the altar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the clause can be explained by the one who holds that הפשט ונתוח are not done on top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says there is no flaying and cutting on top of the altar, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The last answer only works for one opinion, so the גמרא now challenges it from the other opinion. This sets up a new reading of the clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the clause teaches that flaying and cutting may be done on top of the מזבח. But there is an opinion that this is not allowed. For that opinion, the clause cannot mean a regular kosher עולה being flayed on top.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting the animal into its parts
What can be said? A formula for asking how a view explains something

phrases.english: And according to the one who says there is no flaying and cutting
on top of the altar,
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: In other words, how would this opinion explain the clause about flaying and cutting on top?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין הֶפְשֵׁט וְנִתּוּחַ בְּרֹאשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 19 from the opposing opinion
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the clause is about a kosher עולה being flayed on top
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who forbids flaying on top of the מזבח cannot read the clause as permitting it, so the clause needs a different explanation

steps.title: The animal was fit for a moment and then became disqualified
steps.stepSummary: For that opinion, the clause is about an animal that was fit, had its blood sprinkled, and then became פסול. It follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says such an animal is flayed and its skin goes to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where the animal had a time when it was fit and then it became disqualified. This follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who said: once the blood was sprinkled and the meat was accepted for a moment, he should flay it, and its skin goes to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the clause is about an animal that became פסול after its blood was sprinkled. Since it may not go back up if it is taken down, it is flayed right where it is, on top of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a פסול animal is not flayed, since the פסוק says 'אותה', meaning only a kosher one. But רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that once the blood was sprinkled, the offering was accepted for a moment, so it is still flayed and the כהנים get the skin. For this opinion, that is the clause's new teaching, not a rule that flaying is allowed on top of the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here? Introduces a narrower case
A time when it was fit
Its skin goes to the כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the animal was פסול from the start. It was fit, its blood was sprinkled, and only afterward did it become פסול. That one moment of being accepted is why the skin still goes to the כהנים.

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
For example, where it had a time of fitness
and then became disqualified;
and this follows רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון,
who said: once the blood was sprinkled
and the meat was accepted for one moment,
he should flay it, and its skin goes to the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר וְנִפְסְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the clause to a specific case and assigns it to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clause seemed to be about regular flaying of a kosher עולה on top of the מזבח
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about an animal that became פסול after its blood was sprinkled, following רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, so it is flayed and the skin goes to the כהנים
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how both opinions about flaying on top of the מזבח can fit the same משנה.

steps.title: Why take the innards of a disqualified offering down?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the innards are taken down below and rinsed. If the offering is פסול, why bother?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about the teaching: how does he do it? He takes the innards down below and rinses them. Why do I need that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer from a ברייתא about this case, which says to take the innards down and rinse them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the offering is פסול, its innards will never be brought back up onto the מזבח. So taking them down to prepare them for the מזבח seems pointless.

phrases.english: But then, that which is taught: how does he do it?
He takes the innards down below
and rinses them; why do I need this?
phrases.notes: The question here is about taking them down at all, since a פסול offering's innards are never going back up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 21 from a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the animal is פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking innards down to wash them only makes sense if they will be offered, but a פסול offering's innards will not be offered

steps.title: They must be taken down so they are not left with their dung
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the innards obviously must come down, because they cannot be left on the מזבח full of dung. A פסוק in מלאכי shows that something disgusting is not fit for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should we do, offer them with their dung? The פסוק says: "Bring it to your governor; will he be pleased with you or show you favor?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that taking the innards down is clearly needed, since leaving them on the מזבח with their dung would be disgraceful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You would not give a dirty, disgusting gift to a human governor, so it is surely not fitting for the מזבח. So the innards must come off the מזבח. This explains why they are taken down, but not yet why they are rinsed.

phrases.english: What should we do?
Should we offer them with their dung?!
"Bring it now to your governor;
will he be pleased with you or show you favor?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 about why the innards are taken down
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the question is obvious, using a פסוק about disrespect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Taking down a פסול offering's innards seemed pointless
steps.terutzMaskana: They must be taken down because leaving them on the מזבח with dung is disgraceful

steps.title: The real question is why they are rinsed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that its question was not about taking the innards down but about rinsing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we are saying: why do I need to rinse them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies what it really meant to ask. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the innards down makes sense, as step 23 showed. But once they are down and will never go back up, washing them still seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we are saying, a clarification of the question

phrases.english: This is what we are saying:
Why do I need to rinse them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן הָכִי קָאָמְרִינַן מַדִּיחָן לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question of step 22 after step 23's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why innards that will never be offered need to be rinsed
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation in step 21 that the clause is about an offering that became פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the innards are never going back on the מזבח, the ברייתא's instruction to rinse them seems pointless.

steps.title: In case another כהן offers them by mistake
steps.stepSummary: They are rinsed because another כהן might come along, not know they are פסול, and bring them up onto the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if another כהן happens to come and does not know, he will bring them up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for rinsing: a different כהן might not know they are פסול and might bring them up onto the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rinsing is a safety step. If a mistake happens, at least the innards will not go up onto the מזבח with their dung. This ends the defense that the case is a פסול offering, following רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: He will bring them up onto the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: For the view that forbids flaying on top of the מזבח, the clause is about an offering that became פסול after its blood was sprinkled. It is flayed and its skin goes to the כהנים, following רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Its innards are taken down so they do not stay on the מזבח with dung. They are rinsed in case another כהן offers them by mistake.

phrases.english: Because if another priest happens to come along
and does not know, he will bring them up.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי מִיתְרְמֵי כֹּהֵן אַחֲרִינָא וְלָא יָדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clarified question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rinsing protects against another כהן unknowingly offering the innards with their dung
steps.terutzMaskana: Rinsing is a safeguard in case another כהן, not knowing the innards are פסול, brings them up onto the מזבח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rinsing innards that will never be offered seemed unnecessary.
